steps.title: Côte-Rôtie
steps.body: Côte-Rôtie, the roasted slope, lies at the northern end, on very steep schist slopes facing south-east. Its two famous slopes are the Côte Brune, darker, more structured, and the Côte Blonde, lighter, more perfumed. Wines are elegant, floral and peppery. Guigal's single-vineyard La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque made it famous.

steps.title: Hermitage
steps.body: Hermitage is a single, south-facing granite hill above Tain-l'Hermitage. Its reds are powerful, tannic and long-lived, among France's greatest. About a quarter is white, mostly Marsanne, also long-lived. Famous producers include Chapoutier, Jaboulet, with La Chapelle, and Jean-Louis Chave. In the 19th century, Bordeaux was sometimes hermitagé, strengthened with it.
steps.highlight: A single hill, powerful and long-lived

steps.prompt: What are the Côte Brune and Côte Blonde?
steps.explanation: Brune is darker and firmer; Blonde lighter and perfumed.

steps.title: The others
steps.body: Cornas makes dark, rustic, powerful Syrah on granite. Saint-Joseph, a long strip on the west bank, makes lighter, fruitier reds. Crozes-Hermitage, the largest appellation, on flatter land around Hermitage, offers good value. Condrieu and Château-Grillet make Viognier; Saint-Péray, whites and sparkling.

steps.explanation: Gigondas is in the southern Rhône.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Côte-Rôtie is elegant, on Brune and Blonde slopes
Hermitage is a powerful, long-lived single hill
Cornas, Saint-Joseph and Crozes complete the reds
